kept.q: Which of the following statements correctly defines a scalar quantity?
options: A quantity that has magnitude only, with no direction
A quantity that has both magnitude and direction
A quantity that is always added using the parallelogram law
A quantity whose value changes when its direction changes
kept.explanation: A scalar quantity is described completely by its magnitude (size) alone, with no direction attached, e.g. mass, time, and speed. Options B, C and D all describe properties of vector quantities, not scalars.
kept.pidgin: Scalar na quantity wey get size (magnitude) only, e no get direction at all. Examples be mass, time and speed. The other options dey talk about vector wey get direction too.

kept.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
kept.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and a specific direction (e.g. 10 m east), making it a vector. Mass, energy and time are scalar quantities because they only have magnitude.
kept.pidgin: Displacement na vector because e get both size and direction (e dey tell you where the object end up). Mass, energy and time na scalar quantities, dem no get direction.

kept.q: Two forces of magnitude 3 N and 4 N act on a particle such that they are perpendicular to each other. Calculate the magnitude of their resultant force.
kept.explanation: Since the two forces are perpendicular, Pythagoras' theorem applies: Resultant = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt(25) = 5 N. Simply adding or subtracting the forces (giving 7 N or 1 N) is wrong because they do not act along the same line.
kept.pidgin: Since the two forces dey perpendicular (90 degrees to each other), we go use Pythagoras theorem: Resultant = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(25) = 5N. If you just add (7N) or subtract (1N) the forces, e no correct because dem no dey for same line.

kept.q: Chinedu walks 8 m due east and then 6 m due north. Calculate the magnitude of his total displacement from his starting point.
kept.explanation: East and north are perpendicular directions, so Pythagoras' theorem gives the displacement: sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = sqrt(64 + 36) = sqrt(100) = 10 m. Adding the distances directly (14 m) ignores the fact that they are vectors in different directions.
kept.pidgin: East and north dey perpendicular to each other, so we use Pythagoras: sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = sqrt(64+36) = sqrt(100) = 10m. If you just add the two distances (14m), e wrong because na vector quantities wey dey different direction.

kept.q: A force of 20 N acts on an object at an angle of 30 degrees above the horizontal. Using cos30 = sqrt(3)/2 and sin30 = 1/2, calculate the magnitude of the horizontal component of this force.
kept.explanation: The horizontal component of a force is given by F cos(theta) = 20 x cos30 = 20 x (sqrt(3)/2) = 10sqrt(3), which is about 17.3 N. Using sin30 instead of cos30 wrongly gives 10.0 N, which is actually the vertical component.
kept.pidgin: Horizontal component na F cos(theta) = 20 x cos30 = 20 x (sqrt(3)/2) = 10sqrt(3), wey be like 17.3N. If you mistakenly use sin30 you go get 10.0N, but na vertical component be that one.

kept.q: Three forces, P, Q and R, act on a point object and keep it in equilibrium. Which statement correctly describes the vector relationship between these three forces?
options: When drawn head-to-tail in order, P, Q and R form a closed triangle
The sum P + Q + R, when drawn head-to-tail, must always point due north
The three forces must all have exactly equal magnitudes
The three forces must all act along the same straight line
kept.explanation: For an object in equilibrium under three forces, the vector sum of the forces is zero. This means that when the force vectors are drawn head-to-tail (one after another), they form a closed triangle, with no gap left between the start of the first vector and the end of the last. Equal magnitudes or acting on one straight line are not required.
kept.pidgin: If object dey for equilibrium under three forces, e mean say the total (vector sum) of the forces na zero. So if you draw the vectors head-to-tail one after the other, dem go close up well-well make closed triangle. The forces no need to get equal size or dey same straight line.
